title: A Plan of the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans Held alongside an Individual Medicare Advantage Plan
content:
A group retiree Medicare Advantage plan is still a Medicare Advantage plan, so it may not be held alongside an individual one. Every plan of the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans is held on that footing.

## The condition on bringing group coverage into force

No individual Medicare Advantage enrollment is in force for this retiree on the day the group coverage would begin.

The plan's own individual Medicare Advantage enrollment records settle this, before the group coverage is brought into force, read against the retiree the group enrollment names. An individual enrollment standing at disenrolled, at terminated for nonpayment, or at cancelled before it took effect is not in force, and the condition is answered only where every individual Medicare Advantage enrollment that retiree holds stands in one of those three ways.

## Where the retiree does hold an individual plan

Where the retiree holds an individual plan, accepting the group enrollment ends it on the day before the group coverage begins, and the retiree is told what they are giving up before the change is made.

## A drug-only group plan beside an individual medical plan

A drug-only employer group waiver plan and an individual medical plan without drug coverage may be held together, and the plan says which of the retiree's records carries which benefit.

## A Medicare Supplement policy

A retiree who holds a Medicare Supplement policy is told that it pays nothing while a group Medicare Advantage plan is in force, so that they can decide whether to keep paying for it.

## When the group plan ends

A retiree whose group plan ends has a special election period to take an individual plan, and the plan tells them the dates rather than leaving them to find out.
